questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university and the courses, speaking english at the university and the nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall a good experience but the work load was very high.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was fine but the course descriptions did not give that much information about the syllabus, work load and exam form.
All the information was available on UBC's website and some weeks before university started, it was possible to follow a Zoom meeting with more informations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive that much information when i arrived. But if I needed help it was possible to contact Go Global at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was easy and it is possible to get help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not that easy to find cheap places. I rented an Airbnb with two other danish people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is nice to be closer to the city center, but I lived far away from campus. It took me almost 1 hour to go to campus. It is also a bit more difficult to interact with other exchange students. 

I stayed in Mount Pleasant, which is a really nice neighborhood with small cafes and second hand shops. I can recommend staying in this area or Kitsilano which is closer to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is very expensive both living on and off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
All the information was available on UBC's website, and we received a lot of information through mail. 
I got all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for courses some weeks before university started. A list with available courses could be find on UBC's website with a short syllabus and timetable for lectures and other activities. Be aware that the courses can't overlap and some courses are restricted to UBC students. I got all the courses I applied for. It is also possible to switch courses in the first two weeks of study, which gives you a lot of flexibility and opportunity to try different courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think you could write to Go Global if you had problems with the registration. But it was easy to follow the guide and apply for the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You have two weeks in the beginning of the term to switch courses so courses are not binding.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was the same as KU but the work load was higher.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 300 and 400 level courses correspond to third year bachelor academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was kind of the same with lectures and some courses had tutorials or lab. All my courses had one or two midterms, assignments, quizzes and a final exam, which count in the grade. So the work load was high compared to KU. There is no space to fall behind!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MICB 405
MICB 306
MICB 212
BIOC 402

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIOC 402, Proteins: Structure and function. 
The professors were really good and the course was very structured and relevant for my studies.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Car rental

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Vegetables were very expensive in the supermarket, but I found an asian supermarket which was less expensive. 
Housing was very expensive. 
Eating out on restaurants and cafes was a bit less expensive than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many clubs

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could find a club for all activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Outdoor clubs or just going out hiking on your own with friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to Whistler for hiking. I did that almost every week when the weather was good. It was easy to rent a car in Vancouver and just going for a day trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the culture is similar to DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for clubs or other activities through UBC.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many UBC students prioritized their studies much more than I was used to at KU and spent little time socializing in the weekends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Asian food and restaurants.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go hiking in the weekend.
Go second hand shopping!!
Don't slack on your studies

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't bring a lot of clothes - you can find some very nice and cheap clothes in thrift stores.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going hiking in Whistler and the Canadian Rockies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
